evidence: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 now calls FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...) instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. That is a hardcoded cap that ignores admin settings. The higher cap looks deliberate, though: the new block at uploads_controller.rb:63-70 has to receive an oversized image before it can shrink it. The bandwidth risk is also overstated. The download is still bounded at about 10MB (lib/file_helper.rb:18 stops reading once f.size > max_file_size), and lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:81-85 still rejects files over max_#{type}_size_kb. The real costs are that the extra download headroom is fixed rather than derived from settings (for example a multiple of the setting, or the larger of the two settings), and that sites with a limit above 10MB now get truncated downloads.

uploads_controller.rb:65-69 ignores the boolean that OptimizedImage.downsize returns (optimized_image.rb:160-170 convert_with returns false when the exit status is non-zero or an exception is raised). If convert fails, the file does not change and the loop runs convert up to 5 times for nothing. The result is still correct: Upload.create_for and UploadValidator (lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:81-85) reject the oversized file with the normal too_large error, as they did before this PR. The only cost is up to 4 wasted convert calls on the request thread. Breaking out of the loop when downsize returns false is a cheap improvement but not a correctness fix.

git diff --stat shows only 3 files changed (utilities.js, uploads_controller.rb, optimized_image.rb) and no spec files. spec/controllers/uploads_controller_spec.rb has no test that uploads an image larger than max_image_size_kb and checks it is downsized and accepted, or that a non-image over the limit still fails. A spec would also have caught the downsize arity bug in issue 4.

utilities.js:246 hardcodes maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 for HTTP 413. The comment at utilities.js:244 says 413 usually comes from the web server, and config/nginx.sample.conf:61 ships client_max_body_size 10m, so 10MB matches the default deployment. That is arguably more accurate than the old value, max_image_size_kb, which never reflected the web server limit either. The number is still duplicated with the hardcoded 10MB in utilities.js:182 and uploads_controller.rb:55, and sites that set a different proxy limit will see a wrong number. A shared constant or setting would be cleaner, but the message is not more misleading than it was before this PR.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:145-147 defines self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}), and optimized_image.rb:149-151 then redefines self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}). Ruby has no overloading, so the second definition silently replaces the first. The existing caller app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 still calls OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts) with 5 arguments, which now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, given 5, expected 3..4) before optimize runs, so emoji resizing breaks. The failure mode is slightly misdescribed (an ArgumentError at the call, not an error at opts[:allow_animation]), but the bug is real and serious. Fix: give the geometry-string variant a different name, or update resize_emoji.rb to pass "100x100".

spec/models/optimized_image_spec.rb only stubs OptimizedImage.resize (lines 33, 42, 76, 85); no spec calls downsize. Neither the 5-argument call at app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 nor the new geometry-string call at uploads_controller.rb:67 is tested. That gap is why the override regression in issue 4 got through. A small spec for each call pattern (or for the ResizeEmoji job) is worth adding.

utilities.js:182 replaces Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] with a fixed 10 * 1024. For images this is intentional, because the server now downsizes them (uploads_controller.rb:63-70). For non-image attachments it is a regression: nothing downsizes them, and lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:81-85 still rejects files over max_attachment_size_kb (default 3072, config/site_settings.yml:516-518). Users now upload up to 10MB only to be rejected by the server, and when the client check does fire, the alert reports 10MB instead of the configured limit. Fix: keep the per-type setting for attachments and use the relaxed 10MB limit only for image files.
